---
title: "Unemployment in `r params$region`"
subtitle: "Briefing · synthetic data"
params:
  region: "Asir"
format:
  revealjs:
    logo: gastat-logo-color.png
    slide-number: true
---

```{r}
#| include: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tinytable)
rates <- read_csv("unemployment.csv")
area <- rates |> filter(region == params$region)
kingdom <- rates |> filter(region == "Kingdom")
now <- last(area$rate)
change <- now - first(area$rate)
gap <- now - last(kingdom$rate)
```

## The number

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="35%"}
::: {.r-fit-text}
`r scales::number(now, accuracy = 0.1)`%
:::
in 2025 Q4, `r scales::number(change, accuracy = 0.1, style_positive = "plus")`
points since 2022
:::
::: {.column width="65%"}
```{r}
ggplot(area, aes(date, rate)) + geom_line()
```
:::
::::

## Against the Kingdom

::: {.notes}
Ask: what explains the gap?
:::

::: {.incremental}
- Unemployment fell in most regions since 2022
- `r params$region` is `r scales::number(gap, accuracy = 0.1, style_positive = "plus")` points from the Kingdom
:::

## How we know

```{r}
#| echo: true
#| output-location: column-fragment
both <- rates |>
  filter(region %in% c(params$region, "Kingdom"))
ggplot(both, aes(date, rate,
                 colour = region)) +
  geom_line()
```
